body:
Nothing in CI catches a performance regression today. Branch protection on `dev` requires no checks, and the two benchmark workflows, `/perf` and `/bench-compare`, have only failed on `dev`. This PR adds a regression check that can fail CI without false alarms, and stops those two workflows from running on comments.

## Counts, not times

A test can't hold a time to a budget. On GitHub's shared runners, the full test job varied by about 10% across the last five `dev` runs, and the quick job once ran 40% faster than usual. A test can hold a count: the same program does the same work on every machine.

`Evaluator.evaluate_counting_work` is `evaluate`, also returning the steps its trampoline actually took. A reused result counts as the one step that fetches it. That is not `EvaluatorState`'s `step_count`, which counts a reused subtree's steps again to keep probe samples' step bounds in line, so `step_count` is the same with or without reuse. To get the count out, a finished slice (`Trampoline.Yielding.SliceDone`) now carries the run's total steps.

## The budgets

`Test_PerfBudgets` (in the quick suite, under a second) holds two counts to budgets:

| Case | Steps now | Budget |
|---|---:|---:|
| A cold run: recursion, list traversals and case matches (a smaller `bench/eval-bench.hz`) | 206,834 | 227,000 |
| A re-run after an edit to a literal nothing else reads | 378 | 420 |

The re-run must also stay under 5% of a cold run, whatever the budgets. That is the failure our performance work kept finding by hand: a change re-evaluating everything, invisible to tests that check only the answer. With reuse switched off in `IncrEval.reuse_check`, the re-run takes 206,834 steps and the test fails.

Each budget is a ratchet:
- Over it fails, as a regression. Find it, or raise the budget, with the reason in the commit.
- More than a quarter under it also fails, as a stale budget. Lower it in the same change, which records the improvement.

The test's log prints each count (`PERF ...`), so a run shows where they stand.

What a count can't see is a step that got slower. Timings stay in reports, such as `hazel bench-eval`.

## `/perf` and `/bench-compare`

Both now trigger only on manual dispatch, which skips their job, with a comment saying why. They need `bench/build-and-run.sh` and `bench-<sha>` artifacts, which are only on the `perf-bench` branch (#2161), so on `dev` they have only failed. `/perf` also ran a PR's own code for any commenter, with a token that can write to the PR. To revive them, restore the trigger along with what they call.

## Testing

- `PerfBudgets`, `Evaluator`, `WorkerServer`, `ObsBench` and `Stepper` groups: 522 tests pass.
- The counts are the same on repeated runs.
- `dune fmt` is clean, and both workflow files parse.
